mainTopic: Receipts, guarantees (אחריות) in land deeds, and whether rights in a document pass by handing it over (אותיות נקנות במסירה)
overview: The amud opens by defending the general rule that a court writes a שובר (receipt). In the ברייתא's case of stolen land that was sold, a שובר would not protect the later לקוחות (buyers). Either the wrongful collector eats the fruit in the meantime, or a buyer without אחריות never goes back to the seller to find out. Loans are different, because buyers suspect a money debt was already paid and check with the borrower. Next the גמרא asks how a deed is rewritten without its guarantee. רב נחמן gives the wording. From that wording רפרם learns that a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake, and רב אשי disagrees. A story follows in which רב נחמן makes an agent who bought land without a guarantee cover it himself. Finally the גמרא explains the dispute over a returned gift deed, and then a dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about judging by שטר or by חזקה, using the idea of אותיות נקנות במסירה. רב דימי's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Normally we write a receipt, but here it would not help
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא או רב אשי reject the earlier conclusion. Generally a court does write a שובר. Here it is not enough, because the people who could be harmed are the later לקוחות, and they do not hold the שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Generally we do write a receipt. Here, this is the reason we don't: perhaps the creditor will go and take the land from the buyer, and the buyer will then go and take land from other purchasers, and those purchasers do not have the receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier proof from the ברייתא. It says the ברייתא does not prove that a שובר is never written; it has a special reason for this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier inference was: since the ברייתא does not use a שובר, a court never writes one. The answer is that a שובר is written in general, but here it fails, because the chain of collection reaches other לקוחות. The שובר sits with the seller, not with them, so they cannot use it to protect themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing a debt was paid
Creditor; here, the one whose land was stolen

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying a שובר is never written. The point is the opposite: a שובר is normally written, and this case is an exception because it would not reach the people at risk.
steps.whyThisMatters: It saves the general rule that courts write a שובר, and it shows that a protective document only helps if the person at risk actually holds it.

phrases.english: He said to them: generally, we write a receipt,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב פפא or רב אשי, answering the people who drew the conclusion from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and here, this is the reason:
that perhaps the creditor will go
and seize from the purchaser,
and he, the purchaser, will go and seize from other purchasers,
and the receipt is not with the purchasers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn just before this point in the sugya, that courts never write a שובר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the general conclusion drawn from the ברייתא, not the ברייתא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's refusal comes from a case-specific risk (the later לקוחות lack the שובר), not from a general rule against writing a שובר.

steps.title: Won't the purchasers eventually go back to the seller?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. In the end, the harmed purchasers will turn to the owner of the land, the seller, who has the שובר, and the double collection will be exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, don't the purchasers go back to the owner of the land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 1. If the purchasers will eventually reach the seller, the שובר will come out and fix everything, so why worry?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the purchasers lack the שובר. The challenge is that they don't need to hold it themselves: when they claim from the seller, he will show the שובר and the unfair collection will be undone. So the danger seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the land (here, the seller)

phrases.english: Ultimately, the purchasers,
don't they go back to the owner of the land?
phrases.notes: The owner of the land is the seller, who is holding the receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, לָקוֹחוֹת לָאו אַמָּרֵי דְאַרְעָא הָדְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שובר cannot protect the later לקוחות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The purchasers will eventually claim from the seller, who will show the שובר, so the wrong would be discovered and reversed.

steps.title: In the meantime, he takes the land and eats its fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even if the truth comes out later, in the meantime the one who wrongly seized the land holds it and eats its produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, he grabs the land and eats its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 2. The problem will be fixed in the end, but there is real damage in the meantime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a later fix is enough. The answer is that, until the truth comes out, the wrongful collector enjoys the fruit of the land. That loss in the meantime is reason enough not to rely on the שובר.

keyTerms.meaning: In the meantime, while this is going on

phrases.english: In the meantime,
he grabs it and eats the fruit.
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who wrongly took the land; he enjoys its crops until the mistake comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that the wrong is eventually reversed, but points to harm in the meantime.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the purchasers will reach the seller, the שובר eventually protects everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: A later fix is not enough, because the wrongful holder eats the produce in the meantime.

steps.title: A buyer without a guarantee never goes back to the seller
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the concern is about a buyer who bought שלא באחריות. He has no claim against the seller, so he never goes back to him, and the שובר never comes to light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the concern is for a buyer who bought without a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge in step 2. Some buyers will never go back to the seller at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the purchasers going back to the seller. A buyer who bought without אחריות has no right to collect from the seller, so he has no reason to contact him. He never learns that the seller holds a שובר, and the unfair collection is never fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a guarantee; the seller does not promise to repay if the land is taken

steps.whatToRemember: A court generally writes a שובר. In this case it does not rely on one, because the later לקוחות would be harmed: either they lose the fruit in the meantime, or, if they bought without אחריות, they never go back to the seller to find out.

phrases.english: Alternatively, it is about a purchaser without a guarantee.
phrases.notes: Such a buyer can't claim from the seller, so he never goes to him and never sees the receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case to a buyer who has no reason to return to the seller.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every purchaser goes back to the seller, so the שובר will surface.
steps.terutzMaskana: A buyer שלא באחריות never returns to the seller, so the שובר never protects him.

steps.title: Why not worry the same way about loan documents?
steps.stepSummary: If buyers who don't hold the שובר could be harmed, the same worry should stop a court from writing a שובר for loan documents too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should apply to loan documents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. If we worry about harm to later buyers here, we should worry about it with loan documents too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that for a lost loan document, the court does write a שובר. A creditor can also take land from later buyers, and those buyers do not hold the שובר either. So the reason given for the bill of sale seems to apply to loans as well.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reason is true

phrases.english: If so, loan documents too!
phrases.notes: He means: by your reason, a court should not write a שובר for a lost loan document either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reason from steps 1-4 by applying it to loan documents.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the court won't write a שובר because later buyers could be harmed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same risk to buyers exists with loans, yet there the court does write a שובר.

steps.title: A money debt makes the buyer check, a land claim does not
steps.stepSummary: With a loan, a buyer suspects the borrower may have paid in money and checks with him, so the שובר comes out. With a land claim, the buyer knows such claims are not usually settled with money, so he does not check.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, where money is owed, buyers say: maybe the debtor settled with the creditor in money. Here, where land is owed, they know well that someone owed land is not settled with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that loans are different. A buyer facing a money creditor will first ask the borrower if he already paid, but a buyer facing a land claim will not ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loans are normally paid off in cash, so the buyer suspects the debt was already settled and goes to the borrower, who has the שובר. A claim over land is not normally settled with money, so the buyer just gives up the land and never asks. That way the שובר stays hidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The court writes a שובר for a loan but not for a bill of sale, because only with a loan will the buyer go back and the שובר come to light.

phrases.english: There, where he is owed money,
they say: the debtor settled with the creditor in money.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the buyers of the land. They think the loan may already be paid, so they check with the borrower.

phrases.english: Here, where he is owed land,
they surely know that one who is owed land
is not settled with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by showing how loans differ from bills of sale.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The risk to buyers is the same for loans and land sales.
steps.terutzMaskana: With money debts buyers check with the borrower and find the שובר. With land claims they don't, so only there is a שובר not enough.

steps.title: How is a deed written without the guarantee?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's words 'except for the guarantee in it' and asks how such a deed is actually worded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: except for the guarantee in it. How do we write it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the ברייתא. It asks how a court actually writes a new bill of sale that leaves out the guarantee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a court may rewrite a lost bill of sale, but without the guarantee. A guarantee means the seller pays the buyer back if the land is taken away. The גמרא wants the practical wording that removes it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; used to quote a line from an earlier source
Guarantee: the seller pays back the buyer if the land is taken

phrases.english: The Master said:
except for the guarantee that is in it.
How do we write it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חוּץ מִן הָאַחְרָיוּת שֶׁבּוֹ. הֵיכִי כָּתְבִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שובר discussion and returns to a phrase in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording for rewriting a bill of sale without its guarantee.

steps.title: רב נחמן gives the wording
steps.stepSummary: The court writes that this deed cannot be used to collect from any property. It only shows that the land belongs to the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said they write like this: 'This document of ours is not for collecting with, neither from sold property nor from free property, but only so the land stays in the buyer's hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. The new deed openly says it cannot be used to collect anything and only proves the buyer owns the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a bill of sale with a guarantee lets the buyer collect from the seller's property if the land is taken away. The new wording blocks collection from both sold and unsold property. It keeps only one use: proof of ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Mortgaged property, already sold to others
Free property, still owned by the seller

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: they write like this:
'This document of ours is not for collecting with it,
not from sold property and not from free property,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתֵיקוּם אַרְעָא בִּידֵיהּ דְּלוֹקֵחַ״.
phrases.english: but only so that the land stays in the buyer's hands.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deed openly says it cannot be used for collection, only to prove ownership.

steps.title: A missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake
steps.stepSummary: רפרם learns from רב נחמן that a guarantee is assumed in every sale. If the scribe left it out without writing 'no guarantee', the buyer still collects.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: this teaches that leaving out a guarantee is a scribe's mistake. The only reason there is no guarantee is that he wrote so for him. But if he did not write so, the buyer collects.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם draws a general rule from רב נחמן's wording. The guarantee is only removed when the deed says so openly. If the deed just doesn't mention it, it still applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why did רב נחמן need a special clause saying 'not for collecting'? Leaving out the guarantee would not be enough. So a deed that is silent about the guarantee is treated as a scribe's slip, and the buyer can still collect from the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches; introduces a rule learned from what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: A guarantee is part of every land sale by default. It is removed only if the deed openly says so.
steps.confusionAlert: רפרם is not saying the word 'guarantee' is written by mistake. He means that leaving the guarantee out is the mistake, so it still applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting rule: a land sale carries a guarantee even when the deed does not mention it.

phrases.english: Rafram said: this teaches:
a guarantee, it is a scribe's mistake;
phrases.notes: He means: if the guarantee is missing from a deed, we treat it as the scribe's slip, not as the deal.

phrases.english: the reason is that he wrote this for him,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא כְּתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי – גָּבֵי.
phrases.english: but if he did not write this for him, he collects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from רב נחמן's wording in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guarantee is part of every land sale by default; only an open statement removes it, and if it is simply left out the buyer collects.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leaving out a guarantee is a scribe's mistake, so the guarantee still applies.

steps.title: רב אשי: a missing guarantee is not a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that leaving out אחריות is not a טעות סופר. The ברייתא's phrase means the deed simply had no guarantee clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When the guarantee is missing, it is not a scribe's mistake. So what does 'except for the guarantee in it' mean? It means no guarantee was written in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רפרם's rule from step 9. He also gives a new reading of the ברייתא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם, reasoning from רב נחמן's wording, assumed every sale includes a guarantee, even if the scribe forgot to write it. רב אשי says that if it is not written, there is no guarantee. So the ברייתא's words 'except for the guarantee in it' refer to a deed that had no guarantee clause at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee. The seller promises to repay the buyer if the land is taken away, and his other property can be collected from.
'Except for the guarantee in it.' These are the ברייתא's words.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying that a guarantee written in a deed is ignored. He is saying that a guarantee which was never written is not assumed.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A guarantee [that was left out] is not a scribe's mistake,
and what does "except for the guarantee in it" mean?
That no guarantee was written in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אַחְרָיוּת – לָאו טָעוּת סוֹפֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רפרם's rule in step 9 and offers another way to read the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missing guarantee clause means there is no guarantee. The ברייתא's phrase refers to a deed that had no guarantee written in it.

steps.title: An agent buys land without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: A woman sent a man to buy land for her. He bought it without אחריות, and she brought her case to רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman gave money to a certain man so he would buy land for her. He went and bought it for her without a guarantee. She came before רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. This step sets up the case that רב נחמן will rule on in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was acting as her שליח (agent). A purchase without a guarantee is worse for the buyer, because if the land is taken away she gets nothing back. So the question is whether the agent's deal holds.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
who gave money to a certain man
to buy land for her.
He went and bought it for her without a guarantee.
She came before Rav Nachman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דִּיהַבָה לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of guarantees in deeds to a real case about a guarantee in an agent's purchase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What can the woman do, since her agent bought land for her without a guarantee?

steps.title: רב נחמן tells the agent to fix the deal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells the agent that he was sent to help, not to harm. The agent must buy the land himself without a guarantee, then sell it to the woman with his own guarantee.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I sent you to improve things, not to ruin them.' Go buy the land from him without a guarantee, and then sell it to her with a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules on the woman's case. The agent ends up taking on the guarantee himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent who acts against the person who sent him loses his power as an agent. So the purchase does not count as hers. Since the agent agreed to buy without a guarantee, he must take the land himself and sell it to her with a guarantee. That way she gets what she asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I sent you to improve, not to ruin.' This is the rule about an agent who acts against his sender.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of agency. An agent who acts against his sender's interest is not acting as an agent at all.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is speaking to the agent here.

phrases.english: "I sent you to improve things,
phrases.notes: These are the words the woman, as the sender, can say to her agent.

phrases.english: and not to ruin them."
Go buy it from him without a guarantee,
phrases.notes: 'From him' means from the seller of the land.

phrases.english: and then sell it to her with a guarantee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְתַקּוֹנֵי שַׁדַּרְתָּיךָ, וְלָא לְעַוּוֹתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's ruling on the case brought in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The agent must buy the land himself without a guarantee and sell it to the woman with his own guarantee.
steps.whatToRemember: An agent who makes the deal worse for his sender cannot force it on her. Here he has to cover the guarantee himself.

steps.title: Giving back a gift document
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if a gift's receiver gives the document back, the gift goes back too. חכמים say the gift stays with the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If someone gives a gift to his friend, and the friend gives the document back to him, the gift goes back. חכמים say: The gift stays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes a new argument in it, about a gift document that was handed back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether giving back the שטר also gives back the land. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes. חכמים say the gift was already complete, so returning the paper changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document, here the gift deed.
His gift goes back to him.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who gives a gift to his friend,
and he gave the document back to him,
phrases.notes: The person who received the gift hands the deed back to the giver.

phrases.english: his gift goes back.
And the Sages say:
His gift stays.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַנּוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the story to the ברייתא and quotes a new argument in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says returning the gift document cancels the gift. חכמים say the gift stays.

steps.title: Why does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say the gift returns?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why giving back a piece of paper should undo a finished gift. This sets up רב אסי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift is normally final once it is given. So it is surprising that returning the document would cancel it, and the גמרא wants the logic.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first view in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does returning the document cancel the gift?

steps.title: רב אסי: the gift depends on holding the document
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains that it is as if the giver said the field is the receiver's only while he holds the שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: It is as if the giver told him, 'This field is given to you as long as the document is in your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers the question from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the gift is understood as tied to holding the deed. So when the receiver hands the deed back, the condition ends and the field goes back to the giver.

keyTerms.meaning: It is as if he said to him.
As long as the document is in your hand.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the gift lasts only as long as the receiver holds the deed. Giving the deed back ends the gift.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
It is as if he said to him:
"This field is given to you
as long as the document is in your hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, נַעֲשָׂה כְּאוֹמֵר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gift is treated as lasting only while the receiver holds the document. Returning the document ends the gift.

steps.title: רבה challenges Rav Asi: a lost or stolen document should also cancel the gift
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that if the gift depended on holding the שטר, then losing the שטר or having it stolen should also cancel the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: If that is so, then if the document was stolen or lost, the gift should also go back!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the explanation רב אסי just gave for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said the giver meant: 'The field is yours only while the שטר is in your hand.' If that were true, the gift would end whenever the receiver stopped holding the שטר, including through theft or loss. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only spoke about the receiver giving the שטר back, so רב אסי's reason proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (a strong challenge)

phrases.english: Rabba objected to this:
If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the gift really lasts only while the receiver holds the שטר, as רב אסי said.

phrases.english: then if it was stolen or lost, the gift should also go back!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's reason in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that the gift was given only for as long as the receiver holds the שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That condition would also cancel the gift when the שטר is stolen or lost, yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל spoke only of returning it.

steps.title: רבה's new explanation: the argument is about handing over documents
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן disagree about whether אותיות נקנות במסירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: They disagree about whether the rights written in a document pass over just by handing the document over. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that they do, and the רבנן hold that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב אסי's reason failed, רבה offers a completely different reason for the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, handing the שטר back to the giver passes the rights in it back to him, so the field returns. According to the רבנן, simply handing over a document does not pass on those rights, so the gift stays with the receiver. Theft or loss is no problem here, because nobody deliberately handed the document to the giver.

keyTerms.meaning: Letters, meaning the rights written in a document

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of אותיות נקנות במסירה now becomes the key to this dispute, and the גמרא will use it again to explain the next ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
They disagree about whether letters are acquired by handing over.
phrases.notes: 'Letters' means the rights written in the document, and 'handing over' means just giving the paper to someone.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
letters are acquired by handing over,
and the Rabbis hold:
letters are not acquired by handing over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depends on an unspoken condition that the gift lasts only while the receiver holds the שטר
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute depends on whether handing over a document passes on the rights written in it

steps.title: A ברייתא: judging a claim by document or by possession
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי says a person who claims land by both a שטר and a חזקה is judged by the שטר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he is judged by the חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who comes to be judged with a document and with possession is judged by the document; these are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: by the possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל appears again, this time arguing with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person holding land has two claims. One is a שטר of purchase. The other is a חזקה, meaning he lived on the land without challenge for three years. רבי says the court decides based on the שטר, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it decides based on the חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who comes to be judged
Proof of ownership through three years of unchallenged possession

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who comes to be judged with a document and with possession
is judged by the document; these are the words of Rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בַּחֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: by the possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא, which will be linked to the idea from Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: judged by the שטר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: judged by the חזקה.

steps.title: What is the basis of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants to find the reason behind the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the two rulings but not the reasoning behind them. The גמרא is asking for the underlying idea that divides רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The next step gives רב דימי's answer.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in Step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle underlying the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: רב דימי: this dispute is also about handing over documents
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says this dispute also depends on whether אותיות נקנות במסירה. His full explanation continues afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: They disagree about whether letters are acquired by handing over —
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי begins to answer by linking this ברייתא to the same idea רבה used. The text ends here mid-thought, and his explanation of how this works continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the question is whether handing over a document is enough to pass on the rights written in it. Here רב דימי only names the principle. He has not yet explained which side holds what or how it fits the case of שטר and חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
An אמורא known for bringing teachings from ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
They disagree about whether letters are acquired by handing over —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute turns on whether אותיות נקנות במסירה. The details continue in the next lines.
